From Mathlib's Affine/Point.lean I read `map_mk`, `CoordinateRing.map_smul` and the `smul_basis_*` lemmas. The file has two simp lemmas.

- `mapLinear_apply` rewrites the linear-map coercion to the ring hom `map W f`. That is the right direction, since `map` is the canonical form that the other `map_*` simp lemmas (`map_of_X`, `map_root`) are stated for. It cannot loop, because the RHS has no `mapLinear`.
- `map_basisMonomials` has `map W f (basisMonomials W i)` as its LHS with `i` a variable. It applies only when the index is not syntactically a pair. When the index is a literal `(i, j)`, simp rewrites the inner term first with `basisMonomials_apply`. The result then goes through `map_mul`, `map_pow`, `map_of_X` and `map_root`. It reaches the same normal form, `of X ^ i * root ^ j` for `W.map f`, so the two rules don't conflict. I found no cycle.

The `-AdjoinRoot.mk_X` and explicit `map_mk` in the `fin_cases` step (line 127) are a local proof-level workaround. `map_mk` is not a simp lemma in Mathlib, so I found no file-wide simp-interface defect there.
